heard: A galaxy-sized green cloud is glowing with no visible power source. Discovered by Dutch schoolteacher Hanni van Arkel, this phantom sits near the galaxy IC 2497. Located 650 million light years away in Leominer, the structure shines with a striking green glow. Astronomers investigated with the Hubble Space Telescope and found an apparent hole 20,000 light years wide. Yet, nothing inside the massive structure was producing enough energy to light it up. The explanation is terrifying. We are looking at the ghost of a dead quasar. Over 100,000 years ago, a supermassive black hole in IC 2497 blasted a monstrous beam. That powerhouse has since faded dramatically, but its light is still traveling across deep space. Its dead central engine left behind a lingering cosmic ghost.
differences: 'leo minor' heard as 'leominer' after 'years away in'
